metadata.title: Decennium Descent Crafting Bible v4 — Canonical Mechanical Database
notes: All legacy recipes are retained through legacyName and legacyEffect fields.
Legacy monster-part placeholders were replaced with real drops from the uploaded bestiary.
Tools and stations are marked nonconsumable; consumable supplies have values, weights, roles, and tiers.
Generic or mismatched effects were replaced with tradeskill-specific mechanics.
Deep-tier recipe records remain in the internal canonical database but are filtered from player-facing builds by visibility.
metadata.promotedFrom: Decennium_Descent_Crafting_Bible_v2.json (same 687-recipe development lineage used by the v4 standalone book)

visibilityPolicy.public: Recipe/output tier 1–5; available in player runtime and public book.
visibilityPolicy.restricted: Tier 6; archival theory tied to the failed Sixth Gate expedition, excluded from ordinary player runtime.
visibilityPolicy.director-only: Tier 7–10; unknown to the public world and excluded from player builds.

designPillars: EverQuest-style recipe depth: recipes are learned, discovered, traded, researched, and improved rather than improvised from generic gold costs.
Whole-creature utilization: most defeated creatures provide several useful categories such as meat, hide, bone, organs, blood, fat, glands, essence, and specialized structures.
Expedition logistics matter: preservation, weight, tools, time, facilities, and the 240-hour dungeon season create meaningful choices.
Crafting is its own progression: character level grants opportunity, but tradeskill level determines reliable execution.
Materials carry properties: recipes can specify named components or acceptable property combinations.
High-tier crafting remains rare: legendary and mythic recipes require named facilities, research, faction access, Gate zones, or multiseason work.

craftingCheck.formula: d20 + chosen ability modifier + proficiency bonus + tool bonus + facility bonus + assistant bonus
craftingCheck.untrained: A character without the tradeskill or required tool proficiency rolls with disadvantage and cannot attempt recipes above skill level 4.
craftingCheck.assistants: Each qualified assistant adds +1, up to the recipe maximum. Assistants must spend the same active work time.
craftingCheck.takeTen: In a safe workshop, a crafter may use a result of 10 on the die for recipes at least 5 skill levels below their current tradeskill.

qualityOutcomes.effect: Increase yield by 50% or improve one item property; preserve one catalyst.
Increase yield by 25% or improve durability/charges.
Create the listed result.
Create half yield or one reduced-duration/flawed result.
No finished item; recover 25% of non-catalyst materials.
Lose consumed materials and roll on the tradeskill mishap table.

skillAdvancement.gain: First-time crafts and recipes near the crafter’s current level grant the most skill experience. Trivial recipes eventually stop advancing the skill.
skillAdvancement.suggestedXP: 4 XP for first successful craft, 2 XP for a nontrivial repeat, 1 XP for a difficult failed attempt that produces usable research, 0 XP for trivial mass production.
skillAdvancement.levelCost: Advancing a tradeskill level requires 10 + current level skill XP.
skillAdvancement.specialization: At skill level 10, choose one specialty within the tradeskill. Specialty recipes gain +1 and may unlock unique substitutions.

materialTiers.use: Basic carcass parts and ordinary supplies
Specialized organs, quality hides, uncommon minerals
Elite anatomy, magical tissues, refined cores
Ancient scales, heartstones, soul gems, alpha trophies
Mythic cores, pure essences, sentience, worldroot, and campaign-defining components

materialProperties.rule: A property recipe may accept any component of the required tier carrying the listed properties, unless the formula names a specific irreplaceable part.

harvesting.check: Use the creature type’s knowledge skill to identify components, then the relevant gathering tradeskill to remove them.
harvesting.wholeCreatureRule: A successful full harvest normally exposes four to six component categories. The listed bestiary drops are exceptional components, not the only usable remains.
harvesting.partialHarvest: The expedition may take only selected parts, reducing time and weight but forfeiting the remainder.
harvesting.damageSpoilage: The damage type and condition of the corpse can ruin, alter, or improve specific components.
harvesting.sentientRestriction: Humanoid and celestial remains require consent, lawful authority, or explicit dark-path play. Their bodies are not ordinary resource nodes.

preservation.failure: Expired materials lose one quality step per preservation interval and may become contaminated, inert, or dangerous.

stationsAndTime.field: Up to 2 active hours; improvised camp tools; no permanent legendary items.
stationsAndTime.expedition: Up to 8 active hours at a fortified camp or research station.
stationsAndTime.workshop: One to five workdays at a proper dungeon haven or surface facility.
stationsAndTime.haven: One week to one month; requires a named workshop, secure storage, and uninterrupted phases.
stationsAndTime.legacy: More than one month; completed between seasons, by a retired crafter, or through a protected long-term facility.
stationsAndTime.seasonRule: Crafting time represents active work. The 240-hour descent makes long projects strategic commitments rather than free downtime.

recipeDiscovery.formulaRules: Recipes above skill level 4 normally require a formula, schema, pattern, or documented oral tradition.
recipeDiscovery.experimentRules: Experimentation requires a stated desired result, components with relevant properties, a station, and a research check. Failure creates notes and may reveal partial properties.
recipeDiscovery.libraries: Dozens of dungeon libraries preserve formulas, damaged books, false translations, and forbidden research. Some recipes work normally while hiding a second Matrical interpretation.

economy.pricing: Recommended market value includes consumed materials, labor, rarity, risk, and access. Required tools are not consumed.
economy.commission: Standard commissions require a 50% deposit plus all irreplaceable monster parts.
economy.failureRecovery: Ordinary failure recovers 25% of non-catalyst materials; skilled Salvaging can improve this.
economy.antiLoop: Selling crafted goods below an appropriate market or faction demand avoids infinite-profit loops. Repeated mass production can saturate a local market.
economy.retirement: Retired crafters may maintain workshops, teach formulas, complete legacy projects, and improve starting expedition equipment.

matrixResearch.normalRule: Crafting does not automatically reveal the Old Ones’ Matrix.
matrixResearch.qualification: A latent recipe requires one researcher with at least three high-level disciplines among Arcana, History, Religion, Nature, and Engineering plus rare physical evidence.
matrixResearch.function: The recipe’s measurements, ingredient roles, geometry, or alchemical sequence may encode a second meaning.
matrixResearch.timescale: Connecting these anomalies may require many seasons of study in one or more forbidden libraries.
